newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares at mercy of see-sawing Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: German shares at mercy of see-sawing Wall Street.

text.p: German shares dropped sharply on Wednesday, unsettled by losses on Wall Street and disconcerted by the approaching possibility of a German interest rate rise.
The 30-share DAX index ended the bourse session down 84.61 points, or 1.9 percent, at 4,278.48 with losses spread across the board on blue chip stocks.
The afternoon post-bourse session proved a roller-coaster ride, with prices seesawing madly as Wall Street opened firmly, then dropped, and later stabilised again.
The IBIS DAX index finally closed down 3.2 percent at 4,237.06 points, having dropped to a low of 4,211.82.
"People are certainly cautious today," said a dealer at a top Frankfurt bank.
"But the market needed a breather and that's what it is getting. We're not expecting this to go on."
In bourse trade, the market was on hold until U.S. July retail sales and wholesale prices were released in the afternoon, fearing that unfavourable numbers there could steepen Wall Street's decline.
Although the data came through softer than expected, that was not enough to calm the volatile U.S. stock market, which itself fell prey to a drop in Treasuries.

A secondary factor adding to the market's more negative mood were comments from the Bundesbank published this morning which showed the central bank was observing inflation trends closely and would act when necessary.

Dealers said these had been noted by the market but were having no real influence. Financial markets are now broadly of the view that it is only a matter of time before the Bundesbank starts to tighten the monetary policy screws.

Among shares in the news, Hoechst suffered losses in line with the broader market, falling 1.50 marks to 81 marks in bourse trade after the chemical company warned that its 1997 profit would be below 1996 levels.
Other news had minimal impact on share prices.
Deutsche Bank fell 2.20 marks to 117.50 after dismissing as "pure speculation" a press report that suggested it was keen to buy AGF, a French insurer.
